overview: Against the Averbakh set-up Black plays ...f5 at once, challenging e4 and trying to unbalance the position. White usually continues Nf3 and Be2 with a space advantage, while Black gets Dutch-like counterplay but with a weakened e6 and king. It is rare and double-edged.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the big c4-d4-e4 centre with Nf3 and Be2
Exchange on f5 or play e5 to exploit the weak e6 square

black_ideas.idea: Counter in the centre with ...c5 or ...e5

typical_structures.structure: White c4/d4/e4 centre against Black ...f5 and fianchetto

character.notes: ...f5 against a big centre is a risky unbalancing choice.

soundness.notes: Playable but with a doubtful reputation; I am unsure.

structure.notes: The e4/f5 tension tends to open the centre.

level.notes: Needs care but little long theory.
